title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: in this part of the 'Longue Marche' sequel ('variations sur l'équation des lacets'), Grothendieck studies schemes of sections G*_{ρ,σ} (and a tilde-variant G*~_{ρ,σ}). Their sections are tuples (α, β, μ, ε) of 2×2 matrices and scalars. These are local solutions of a 'loop equation' relating α, its conjugate twisted by ρ, β twisted by σ, and a sign ε. Two auxiliary groups appear: an upper-triangular-type group B'_0 with elements u, and a subgroup N'_σ.

The page finishes the remark begun on p. 318: a section is determined by α alone, modulo N'_σ.
- From α one gets u, hence μ = det u.
- β is then of the form β = u b^{-1}, with b an arbitrary local section of N'_σ.
- The sign is then ε = ε(b).
- The condition for α to extend to a section is that the D-entry of ξ = αρ(α)^{-1} = αρα^{-1}ρ^{-1} (a group commutator) be invertible. Then μ = 1/D, numbered (33)-(34).

He makes this explicit with α = (a b; c d), δ = det α = ad − bc, and ρ = (0 1; v 1), so det ρ = −v and tr ρ = 1. He groups the product as ξ = (αρ)(α^{-1}ρ^{-1}), with αρ = (bv, a+b; dv, c+d) and α^{-1}ρ^{-1} = −(1/δv)(d+bv, −d; −c−av, c). This gives (36):
- (−δv)A = vb(d+vb) − (a+b)(c+va)
- (−δv)B = −vbd + c(a+b)
- (−δv)C = vd(d+vb) − (c+d)(c+va)
- (−δv)D = −vd² + cd + c²

The key quantity (37) is (−δv)D = c² + cd − vd² = det(dρ + c·1). This is the norm form of the quadratic algebra Z[ρ] = Z[x]/(x² − x − v), evaluated at c + dρ. So the extension condition is that the bottom row (c, d) of α define a unit c + dρ in the quadratic algebra generated by ρ.

The next page uses this to write u = (1/D, B/D; 0, 1) explicitly in terms of a, b, c, d. It also asks to what extent (β, ε) instead of α determine μ.

This is a routine explicit computation within Grothendieck's case-study of the loop equation for GL2/PGL2-type data.
errors: No errors in the computation on this page: (36) and (37) check out entry by entry, and det(c + dρ) = c² + cd·tr ρ + d² det ρ = c² + cd − vd² confirms (37). (On the next page as transcribed, the denominator '−vd²+cd+d²' should read '−vd²+cd+c²'; that is likely a transcription slip, not Grothendieck's.)

ideas.what: Parametrising local sections of the solution scheme G*_{ρ,σ} of the loop equation by α modulo N'_σ, with the obstruction to extension being invertibility of one matrix entry D of the commutator αρα^{-1}ρ^{-1}
ideas.modern_name: explicit description of a torsor / solution scheme of a twisted-conjugacy (cocycle) equation in GL2

ideas.what: The extension condition expressed as a norm: (−δv)D = det(c + dρ) = N(c + dλ) with λ² − λ − v = 0
ideas.modern_name: norm form of a quadratic order (binary quadratic form c² + cd − vd²)

deep.surprise_reason: A correct, routine explicit matrix computation inside a larger unpublished case study. The norm-form interpretation is elementary, and there is no evident new result or connection.
transcription_corrections: Top of page: the page number '350' (Grothendieck's own numbering) is correct.
(37): the right-hand side reads 'det(dρ + c)' (i.e. det(c·1 + d·ρ)), not 'det(αρ + c)'.
The last line is a struck 'et après calcul où' replaced by 'où δ = det α = ad − bc et v le paramètre qui définit ρ = (0 1; v 1)'. This matches the transcription; there is no extra content.
